nodes.rationale: SciMLSensitivity team's current general recommendation for reverse-mode AD with many parameters: O(n^3+p) vs O((n+p)^3) for BacksolveAdjoint/InterpolatingAdjoint, supports checkpointing, avoids backwards-solve instability on stiff systems/DAEs that breaks BacksolveAdjoint.

nodes.rationale: Closest Python counterpart to Catalyst.jl's SBML-based simulation path (libRoadRunner LLVM-JIT solver), but lacks Catalyst+ModelingToolkit's symbolic modeling depth -- bridge via juliacall for symbolic features.

nodes.label: Pigeons.jl (NRPT)
nodes.rationale: Non-reversible parallel tempering biases swap proposals so replicas drift monotonically along the temperature ladder, achieving order-of-magnitude better round-trip rate than standard reversible PT.

nodes.label: freud (Glotzer group)
nodes.rationale: Fastest single-frame RDF/S(q)/Steinhardt analysis with GPU-ready neighbor-list infrastructure reused across analyzers; does not read trajectory files itself, so typically paired with MDAnalysis/MDTraj as the frame iterator.

nodes.label: BifurcationKit.jl
nodes.rationale: Blocked on Julia 1.12: MiniQhull >=0.4 dependency fails to build across all OSes. AUTO-07p (Fortran) recommended as working alternative for continuation today; BifurcationKit.jl code retained only for reference / older Julia installs.

nodes.label: MIPROv2 optimizer
nodes.rationale: Bayesian optimization over instructions + exemplars + demonstrations; current state-of-the-art general-purpose DSPy optimizer. Escalate budget (auto=heavy) only when dev-set gain justifies token spend.

nodes.label: PySINDy
nodes.rationale: No mature JAX-native SINDy library exists; for a JAX-first workflow, hand-roll STLSQ via jax.lax.scan, or bridge via PySR's model.jax() exporter.

nodes.label: Non-centered reparameterization
nodes.rationale: Classic fix for funnel geometries in hierarchical models -- sampling a standard-normal z and transforming (y = mu + sigma*z) instead of sampling y directly avoids narrow-funnel pathologies as sigma approaches 0.

nodes.label: Covalent Adaptable Networks (Vitrimers)
nodes.rationale: A well-designed vitrimer maintains constant crosslink density and instead behaves like a viscosity dependent on exchange-reaction rate; this is why vitrimers can be reprocessed like thermoplastics while retaining thermoset-like properties at use temperature.

nodes.label: Green-Tobolsky Model
nodes.rationale: Vitrimers show Arrhenius (not WLF) temperature dependence of viscosity because relaxation is set by the bond-exchange reaction rate rather than reptation/segmental motion — this is the primary diagnostic distinguishing vitrimer behavior from conventional polymer melt rheology.

nodes.label: Physical Networks
nodes.rationale: Physical networks can flow and dissolve because crosslink density itself drops if reversible bonds don't reform after breaking.
